at åbne.explanation: "At åbne" means "to open". You can open a door, a shop or a bank account. Hvornår åbner I? (When do you open?) is what you ask a shop or office.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **åbne** døren for dig.
sentence.en: I want to open the door for you.

at åbne op.explanation: "At åbne op" means "to open up": Hun åbner op om sine følelser (She opens up about her feelings). It also fits shops: Butikken åbner op klokken ni (The shop opens at nine).

sentence.da: Kan du **åbne op**? Jeg står udenfor.
sentence.en: Can you open up? I am standing outside.

at ånde.explanation: "At ånde" means "to breathe", but it is more literary than everyday. In speech Danes say at trække vejret (to breathe): Jeg kan ikke trække vejret (I cannot breathe). At ånde combines with ind (in) and ud (out): at ånde ud (to breathe out).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **ånde** i så tyk røg.
sentence.en: It is hard to breathe in such thick smoke.

en å.explanation: "En å" means "a stream", a small river. Do not mix it up with en flod (a bigger river): Floden er bredere (The river is wider).

sentence.da: Vi gik en tur langs den smalle **å**.
sentence.en: We took a walk along the narrow stream.

en åbning.explanation: "En åbning" means "an opening", a gap in something. It is also the start of an event or a shop: Vi går til åbningen (We are going to the opening).

sentence.da: Katten fandt en lille **åbning** i hegnet.
sentence.en: The cat found a small opening in the fence.

en åbningsdag.explanation: "En åbningsdag" means "an opening day", the first day a shop, a restaurant or an event is open to the public. Shops often have an åbningstilbud (opening offer) then.

sentence.da: Der var lang kø foran butikken på dens **åbningsdag**.
sentence.en: There was a long line in front of the shop on its opening day.

en åbningstid.explanation: "En åbningstid" means "an opening hour". Danes usually say it in the plural when they ask when a shop is open: Hvad er butikkens åbningstider? (What are the shop's opening hours?)

sentence.da: Butikkens **åbningstid** er fra ni til fem.
sentence.en: The shop's opening hours are from nine to five.

en åkande.explanation: "En åkande" means "a water lily", a plant that grows in still water and has large white or yellow blossoms.

sentence.da: En **åkande** har runde blade, der flyder på vandet.
sentence.en: A water lily has round leaves that float on the water.

en ål.explanation: "En ål" means "an eel", a long, thin fish with a smooth body. The plural stays the same: to ål (two eels).

sentence.da: En **ål** lever i vand og ligner en slange.
sentence.en: An eel lives in water and looks like a snake.

en ånd.explanation: "En ånd" means "a spirit", a being without a body that people believe in or tell stories about. It also means the general attitude of something: lovens ånd (the spirit of the law).

sentence.da: Børnene tror, at der bor en **ånd** i det gamle hus.
sentence.en: The children believe that a spirit lives in the old house.

en årring.explanation: "En årring" means "a tree ring", one of the circles you see when a tree is cut across. It is built from år (year) and ring (ring).

sentence.da: Hver **årring** i stammen viser et år i træets liv.
sentence.en: Each tree ring in the trunk shows one year in the tree's life.

en årsag.explanation: "En årsag" means "a reason", the cause of something that happened. For a reason to do something, use en grund (a reason): Jeg har en god grund til at blive hjemme (I have a good reason to stay home).

sentence.da: Der må være en **årsag** til, at bilen ikke starter.
sentence.en: There must be a reason why the car does not start.

en årsopgørelse.explanation: "En årsopgørelse" means "an annual tax statement", the yearly statement from the Danish Tax Agency showing what you earned and whether you paid too much or too little. It is usually available online in the spring.

sentence.da: Jeg kan se på min **årsopgørelse**, at jeg får penge tilbage.
sentence.en: I can see on my annual statement that I get money back.

en årstid.explanation: "En årstid" means "a season", one of the four parts of the year. Do not mix it up with en sæson (a season of a show or sport): Sæsonen starter i dag (The season starts today).

sentence.da: Vinter er en kold **årstid**, og sommer er en varm.
sentence.en: Winter is a cold season, and summer is a warm one.

et åbent hus.explanation: "Et åbent hus" means "an open house", an event where anyone can come and look around. It is used for schools, companies and homes for sale.

sentence.da: Skolen holder **åbent hus** på lørdag.
sentence.en: The school has an open house on Saturday.

et år.explanation: "Et år" means "a year". It is also how you give your age: Jeg er tredive år gammel means "I am thirty years old".

sentence.da: Der er tolv måneder i et **år**.
sentence.en: There are twelve months in a year.

et århundrede.explanation: "Et århundrede" means "a century", a hundred years. It is built from år (year) and hundrede (hundred). Dates use it: i det 21. århundrede (in the 21st century).

sentence.da: Huset er næsten et **århundrede** gammelt.
sentence.en: The house is almost a century old.

et årstal.explanation: "Et årstal" means "a year", the number that names a year, like 1990. For a length of time, use et år: tre år (three years).

sentence.da: Hvilket **årstal** blev huset bygget?
sentence.en: Which year was the house built?

et årti.explanation: "Et årti" means "a decade", a period of ten years: de sidste to årtier (the last two decades). Danes name a decade by its tens, for example firserne (the eighties).

sentence.da: Vi har boet her i mere end et **årti**.
sentence.en: We have lived here for more than a decade.

åben.explanation: "Åben" means "open", for doors, shops and windows. At åbne (to open) is the action: Jeg åbner døren (I open the door).

sentence.da: Butikken er **åben** til klokken seks.
sentence.en: The shop is open until six o'clock.

åbenbart.explanation: "Åbenbart" means "apparently" and is used when you work something out from what you see or hear. Compare tydeligvis (clearly), which sounds more sure.

sentence.da: Han er **åbenbart** syg i dag.
sentence.en: He is apparently sick today.

åbenlys.explanation: "Åbenlys" means "obvious", so plain that nobody can miss it. It is built from åben (open) and lys (light): out in the open, for everyone to see. It is often used about faults and lies.

sentence.da: Hans løgn var **åbenlys**, og alle kunne se det.
sentence.en: His lie was obvious, and everyone could see it.

åbningstider.explanation: "Åbningstider" means "opening hours". It is built from åbning (opening) and tider (times). You often see it on shop doors and museum websites.

sentence.da: Butikkens **åbningstider** er fra ni til seks.
sentence.en: The shop's opening hours are from nine to six.

åndelig.explanation: "Åndelig" means "spiritual", about the mind and spirit as opposed to the body. It comes from en ånd (a spirit). For mental health, Danes say psykisk (mental), not åndelig.

sentence.da: Hun søger ro og **åndelig** styrke i naturen.
sentence.en: She seeks peace and spiritual strength in nature.

årlig.explanation: "Årlig" means "annual", something that happens once a year. Det sker årligt (It happens every year) says how often.

sentence.da: Vi har en **årlig** fest i juni.
sentence.en: We have an annual party in June.

årvågen.explanation: "Årvågen" means "alert" or "vigilant", watching closely and ready to notice danger or small changes. The last part, vågen, means awake: Jeg er vågen (I am awake).

sentence.da: Natvagten må være **årvågen** og lægge mærke til alt.
sentence.en: The night guard must be alert and notice everything.
